questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to experience a new culture different from what we are used to in Denmark. I wanted to visit a country with the possibility to travel during my free time but also be enrolled in a high-ranked university to achieve the highest possible learning outcome combined with my cultural experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Good orientation week

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Got relevant e-mails, brochures etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have been more events just for exchange students since we had orientation with all new uni students as well

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not hard but expensive. Since I was traveling with my partner, we ended up renting an airbnb instead of having to buy furniture etc. Student housing would have been cheaper

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living on campus as an exchange student would probably have encouraged more social event so could be recommend if traveling alone

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really look into it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was easy since you can find all relevant courses on the university webpage before you are enrolled but I remember it was a bit late in the process that you could choose the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact with the faculty but was a bit hard being abroad. Good that you are able to change your courses during the first week so you are sure to make the right choice. However, a lot of the courses were full so better to choose the right courses upon registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them but some teaching time tables changes which led to overlapping courses. I ended up changing one course after trying it the first week which was a good option. The overlapping course was available online and could be viewed as a recording so it was find. However, this is not possible for all course and information about this option was hard to get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to choose the courses you like the most in the beginning because it can be hard to change if they are full afterwards. If courses are overlapping, maybe contact the course coordinator to ask if it will be available as a recording. Be aware of any overlapping exams. It was possible to find student comments about the courses in their Facebook group which could have been nice to see before choosing the courses. It was called VUWLSS for law students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High level and workload. A lot of reading for the law courses but probably since it is a common law country. However, it definitely depends on the different kinds of courses. Several students only take 3 courses instead of 4 to help with the workload but this option is not possible for exchange students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A mixture of seminars and lectures, pretty similar to law courses in Copenhagen. However, the exams and essays were different from what we are used to but you can take optional workshops to learn more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAWS 334 - Ethics and the law
LAWS 340 - International law
LAWS 380 - Evidence
LAWS 394 - Special Topic: The Treaty of Waitangi in New Zealand Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: LAWS 380 - Evidence was an interesting class for people interested in criminal law. LAWS 340 - International law had a level too high for the credits provided and too much reading but a really interesting course.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery stores, rent, and food was very expensive in general. You didn't really have to buy books since the material was also provided online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good option for being part of clubs. The gym/fitness at my campus wan't really that nice but cheap. I heard it was better at the other campuses which you could also use.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different social and athletic clubs - a long list can be found on the website. I joined the international leadership programme and the international buddy programme which I can recommend,

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International buddy programme so you can meet other international students and have a buddy to ask for advice

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try traveling as much as you can around the country before/after your stay or during the break. Wellington is located far away from other big cities but you can do hikes or activities in the city. I really enjoyed Somes island on a sunny day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their accent

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) research your causes before signing up, 2) buy a car and sell it again before you leave if you can stay at a place with parking to do roadtrips, 3) book your flights early since they can be expensive and also the ferry ticket to the South Island if you plan on going by car

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to live in a different country, embracing their culture, and making new connections

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from friends and family

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
